model: Bank FCFE at cost of equity (engine route), net debt zero, CET1 retention on risk-weighted-asset growth, perpetual-bond coupons charged in the flow

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: terminal nominal growth for a low-ROE Chinese joint-stock bank whose balance sheet can only grow ~3%/yr at a 30% payout without eroding CET1; bracketed by revenue 5yr CAGR -5.1% and BVPS 5yr CAGR 4.2%. Base revenue path 3.0% -> 2.5%.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity attributable to equity holders 3yr/5yr CAGR 4.8%/5.4% vs revenue 0.1%/-5.1% and EPS -3.9%/-2.4% (>30% apart, opposite sign). Equity growth is retained earnings at a ~30% payout plus RMB30bn of net new perpetual bonds (other equity instruments 95.8bn FY2024 -> 125.0bn FY2025), not operating growth. Revenue fell from 181.8bn (FY2020) to 139.7bn (FY2025) as NIM compressed 2.14% -> 1.40%. Equity CAGR is NOT used as the growth rate.
historical_growth.notes: FCF CAGRs are null: a bank's reported FCF is deposit-flow noise (OCF -231.6bn FY2024, -157.5bn FY2025, +184.2bn H1 2026). The relevant series is net profit to ordinary shareholders, 27,451 FY2025 (FY2024 equity-holder profit 32,296 less 3,440 coupons = ~28,856), falling again in H1 2026 (17,347 vs ~19,880). BVPS 10.50 (FY2020) -> 12.90 (FY2025) -> 13.24 (H1 2026). ROE 14.0% (FY2017) -> 4.93% (FY2025).

scenario_narratives.base: NIM holds ~1.45-1.5%, credit cost eases from ~1.4% to ~1.15%, operating income grows ~3% and RWA ~3%. FCFE rises from ~RMB6bn (FY2026E) to ~RMB9bn (FY2027) and ~RMB22bn by FY2036, roughly covering a ~30% payout throughout with CET1 flat at 9.4%. Terminal ROE ~5.4%, implied terminal P/B ~0.34x.
scenario_narratives.bull: The credit cycle turns: NIM recovers a further 5-10bp, credit cost falls toward 1.0%, PBT margin returns to ~30%, revenue grows ~4%. FCFE ~RMB9bn in FY2027 rising to ~RMB27bn; terminal ROE ~6.5% -- still below the cost of equity.
scenario_narratives.bear: Credit cost stays ~1.5% on retail and residual property losses while NIM compresses again; revenue falls 1% then stalls; RWA keeps growing on policy lending so FCFE is ~RMB3bn for two years, below the dividend. Either the payout is cut or a discounted raise dilutes; terminal ROE ~3.8%.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A bank is worth the equity cash flow it can distribute after funding its own capital requirement, discounted at the cost of equity. For Minsheng that flow is net profit to ordinary shareholders (after tax, NCI and perpetual-bond coupons) less the equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on growing risk-weighted assets. Unlike China CITIC Bank, Minsheng's ~30% dividend is roughly covered by that FCFE -- CET1 has been flat because RWA growth has been held to ~2-3% -- but the flow is small because ROE is only ~5%. Net debt is zero by construction; deposits are operating funding. The H share trades at 0.21x book; the base case implies a terminal P/B of ~0.34x, consistent with a ~5.4% ROE at an 11% cost of equity. The valuation is a bet on how cheaply a low-return bank is priced, not on it earning its cost of capital.
key_risks_to_valuation: Credit cycle: impairment losses were 38.6% of operating income in FY2025 and 42.7% in H1 2026 (annualised credit cost ~1.4% of loans); management flags retail as the pressure point and personal loans shrank 4.5% in H1 2026. A further rise in credit cost takes PBT margin below 18% and FCFE near zero (bear case).

Capital: CET1 9.42% is ~1.7pt above the 7.75% D-SIB minimum. ROE ~5% at a 30% payout only funds ~3% RWA growth; faster policy-directed lending or a credit loss forces a dividend cut or a discounted raise that the flat share count does not model.
NIM: 2.14% (FY2020) to 1.39% (FY2024-H1 2025), recovering to 1.47% in H1 2026. Management expects margin pressure to persist; a reversal removes the base case's revenue growth.
Low profitability is structural: ROE 4.9% vs an 11% cost of equity means every retained yuan destroys value at book; the case for upside rests on the 0.21x P/B starting point, not on growth.

Governance and currency: no controlling state shareholder (dispersed private ownership with Dajia/Anbang legacy stakes), payout set at ~30% by policy, no buyback lever; RMB flows against an HKD quote -- a 10% RMB move is a 10% move in the HKD value; 10% H-share dividend withholding tax is not modelled.
Cost of equity: 11.0% is a judgment; at 10% the base value rises ~15%, at 12% it falls ~12% (sensitivity grid: HKD 5.48 at 10%, 4.21 at 12%).

data_sources.price: Yahoo Finance chart API (1988.HK, HKD) at inputs.price_as_of; 52-week range 3.09-4.46. FX CNYHKD=X, USDCNY=X, USDHKD=X and the A share 600016.SS from the same API on the same date.
data_sources.financials: 1988.HK_Metrics.csv / metrics_normalized (FY2017-FY2025 annual, H1/Q interim to H1 2026, RMB millions) built from the HKEX annual, interim and quarterly reports in Extracted/; kpis table for NIM, NPL, coverage, CET1, total capital ratio, credit impairment, ordinary shareholders' equity, BVPS, dividends, ROE. FY2025 annual report: profit distribution (RMB8,274m = 30.14% of ordinary profit 27,451m, line 7740-7752), capital table (RWA 6,011,048, line 3335), perpetual-bond interest (line 9150), tax and NCI (line 8921-8929). H1 2026 interim: key indicators and capital (p.7-8, lines 300-390; CET1 9.42%, RWA 6,142,309), interim dividend RMB1.18/10 shares = 29.78% of ordinary profit 17,347m (lines 4928-4940), prospects (p.73, line 3357).
data_sources.qualitative: 1988.HK_Analysis.json was not yet written when the drivers were set; it landed before the final build and was read: it CONFIRMS the drivers without moving any path (no numeric FY2026 guidance, only industry-wide stability; real-estate exposure ~RMB325bn flagged high severity; Dajia ~17.8% largest holder, no controlling shareholder; CET1 ~9.4% below state-bank peers constrains growth/dividend). Outlook and risk context taken directly from the H1 2026 interim 'Prospects' section and the FY2025 annual report.

inputs.base_revenue_note: FY2026E operating income, RMB m: H1 2026 actual 73,695 (interim p.7, +4.2% YoY; NII +6.9% on NIM 1.47% vs 1.39%) + H2 2026E 71,000 (FY2025 H2 actual 68,976 x ~1.03). FY2025 actual 139,677. Operating income = net interest income + net non-interest income, the Bank's headline revenue line.
inputs.share_count_basis: 43,782 million A + H ordinary shares in issue at 30 June 2026 (interim p.8 share capital 43,782; unchanged since FY2017). One class, identical economic rights, so the per-share value applies to the H share. Held FLAT: no buybacks (ShareRepurchases 0 every year), no share scheme (SBC-zero), no convertible outstanding. A discounted recapitalisation is the dilution risk the flat count ignores (bear case narrative).
inputs.debt_cash_note: Bank: customer deposits (RMB4.39tn at 30 Jun 2026), central-bank borrowings, interbank funding and debt securities issued are operating funding; cash and central-bank balances are liquidity reserves, not surplus. Net debt is zero by construction on the FCFE route; nothing is bridged after the flows. The RMB125bn of perpetual bonds (other equity instruments) is charged through its coupons in cash_tax_rate_path, not deducted as debt.
inputs.fcf_note: last_fcf is FY2026E FCFE = net profit attributable to ORDINARY shareholders ~24,100 (H1 actual 17,347 + H2E ~6,750; FY2025 27,451) LESS capital retained to hold CET1 at ~9.4% on RWA growth from 6,011bn to ~6,200bn (0.094 x 189,000 = ~17,800). Reported OCF - capex (FY2025: -157,476 - 9,299; H1 2026 +184,168) is deposit and interbank flow noise and is not used.
inputs.sbc_source: SBC-zero: no share-based payment scheme in the FY2018-FY2025 annual reports (StockBasedComp 0, EquityAwardTaxes 0, ShareRepurchases 0 every period in the CSV); basic = diluted EPS (RMB0.63 FY2025, 0.40 H1 2026). House and street bases coincide; band_position is degenerate.
inputs.fx_note: fx_rate converts CNY (model; the Bank reports in RMB) to HKD (H-share quote): 1 CNY = 1.1724 HKD, Yahoo CNYHKD=X at 2026-10-16T22:02Z. Direction check: HKD is the weaker unit (USDHKD 7.8479 vs USDCNY 6.6768), so HKD per CNY must exceed 1 -- triangulated 7.8479 / 6.6768 = 1.1754, same source and date, within 0.3%. Dual-listing check: Shanghai A share 600016.SS closed CNY 3.50 = HKD 4.10, a ~24% premium to the H share at inputs.price_as_of that is normal for Chinese banks, so the A line is not a parity anchor. The engine values the flows in CNY and multiplies the per-share value by fx_rate to get HKD.
inputs.price_as_of: 2026-10-16T08:08:14Z regular close (HKEX), Yahoo Finance chart API
inputs.wacc_rationale: Cost of equity 11.0% in CNY terms, applied to CNY flows: China 10y government bond ~1.8-2.0% + equity risk premium for a Chinese joint-stock bank ~9% (beta ~1.1-1.2 on a ~7.5% China ERP). Set 0.5pt above the 10.5% used for China CITIC Bank (0998.HK) and 1.5pt above CCB (0939.HK, 9.5%): Minsheng is a privately-originated joint-stock bank without a state or SOE-conglomerate anchor shareholder, its ROE (4.9% FY2025, 6.05% annualised H1 2026) is the lowest of the national joint-stock banks, it carried the heaviest property-developer exposure of the group through 2021-24, and credit impairment rose 20.8% YoY in H1 2026. No WACC: deposits are operating funding, so the equity flow is discounted at the cost of equity.
inputs.lease_treatment: Not material: lease liabilities RMB8.1bn (FY2025) against RMB7.8tn of assets; IFRS 16 depreciation and interest already sit inside operating expenses and hence inside the pre-tax margin. No separate lease charge.
inputs.nci_treatment: NCI is immaterial (RMB19m of FY2025 profit; slightly negative in H1 2026) and is folded into cash_tax_rate_path together with income tax and perpetual-bond coupons, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = profit to ordinary shareholders.
inputs.notes: MODEL CHOICE: routed via .claude/skills/dcf-methods/SKILL.md -- a bank is not valued on owner FCF (deposits are not net debt; OCF is deposit-flow noise). Valued as FCFE at the cost of equity on the engine route, the same construction used for the closest comparable China CITIC Bank (0998.HK, 2026-10-12): revenue = operating income; ebitda_margin_path = PROFIT BEFORE TAX / operating income (i.e. after operating expenses AND credit impairment, which is the real cost of a bank); sbc, D&A, leases and working capital all zero; cash_tax_rate = income tax + NCI + perpetual-bond coupons as a share of PBT, so EBIT x (1 - rate) = net profit to ORDINARY shareholders; capex = equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on RWA growth (g_RWA x 9.4% x prior-year RWA, as % of revenue), so FCF = FCFE = distributable earnings. Net debt zero. KEY FINDING vs 0998.HK: at Minsheng the dividend is roughly COVERED by FCFE, not funded by capital drift -- CET1 has been flat-to-up (9.28% FY2023, 9.36% FY2024, 9.38% FY2025, 9.42% H1 2026) because RWA growth has been held to 1.6% (FY2024) and 2.9% (FY2025), and the ~30% payout (FY2025 RMB8,274m = 30.14% of ordinary profit 27,451m; H1 2026 interim RMB5,166m = 29.78%) retains just enough to fund that growth. The binding constraint is the opposite: ROE is so low (4.9% FY2025) that the balance sheet can only grow ~3%/yr at a 30% payout without eroding CET1. CET1 9.42% sits ~1.7pt above the 7.75% D-SIB minimum (7.5% + 0.25% surcharge); there is little room to let it drift. EARNINGS TREND: PBT margin has fallen from 36-41% (FY2017-19) to 23.1% (FY2025) and ~20.5% FY2026E; credit impairment was 38.6% of operating income in FY2025 and 42.7% in H1 2026 (annualised credit cost ~1.4% of loans) while NIM recovered 8bp YoY to 1.47% and cost-to-income fell to 27.8%. Profit is heavily H1-weighted (FY2025 PBT H1 22,794 vs H2 9,465), so FY2026E ordinary profit ~24,100 is below FY2025. Management's H2 2026 prospects (interim p.73): 'slower but higher-quality' loan growth as the new normal, margin pressure persisting, 'retail business will face relatively greater risk pressure' -- no numeric targets. Personal loans shrank 4.5% in H1 2026 while corporate grew 5.6%. QUALITATIVE CONTEXT: 1988.HK_Analysis.json was not present when the drivers were set; the drivers rest on the FY2025 annual and H1 2026 interim and the kpis table. VALUATION TIMING: valuation date is 9.5 months into FY2026, so FY2026E is fy0 (not discounted) and the first discounted flow is FY2027; the FY2025 final dividend (paid Jul/Aug 2026) and FY2026 interim (RMB5,166m, Dec 2026) come out of fy0 and are not double-counted. H-share dividends carry 10% withholding tax for non-resident individuals, not modelled. H share trades at 0.21x H1 2026 BVPS (RMB13.24 = HKD15.52) and ~6.7% trailing yield.

bear.growth_rationale: The H1 2026 NIM rebound reverses on further LPR cuts while deposit costs stick (management: 'limited room for further decrease in deposit costs'); the FY2020-25 revenue decline (-5%/yr) slows to flat then low growth.
bear.margin_rationale: Credit cost stays ~1.5% for two years on retail (personal loans already shrinking 4.5% in H1 2026, management flags 'greater risk pressure' in retail) and residual property/LGFV losses; PBT margin troughs at 17% then recovers only to 21%, below FY2025.
bear.capex_rationale: Policy-directed lending keeps RWA growing 3.0% for three years even as revenue falls, then 2.5% and 2.0%; holding CET1 at 9.4% absorbs ~85% of ordinary profit in FY2027-28 (FCFE ~RMB3bn against a ~RMB6-7bn dividend). This is the scenario where the dividend is cut or a discounted recapitalisation dilutes H-share holders; the flat share count understates that damage. Terminal ROE ~3.8%.
bear.tax_rationale: Fixed perpetual-bond coupons (~RMB4bn) against a smaller PBT.
bear.terminal_note: Gordon 1.02/0.09 = 11.3x FCFE; cap does not bind. Implied terminal P/B ~0.2x on ROE ~3.8%.
bear.narrative: A prolonged credit-cost cycle plus renewed NIM compression. Ordinary profit falls to ~RMB20bn, CET1 cannot fund both 3% RWA growth and a 30% payout, and value accrues to policy lending rather than minority H-share holders.

base.growth_rationale: Operating income +3.0% then 2.5%: NIM has stabilised (1.47% H1 2026, +8bp YoY, first rise after falling from 2.14% in FY2020) but management expects margin pressure to persist; loans growing ~2-3% ('slower but higher-quality'), non-interest income flat (H1 2026 -1.8%).
base.margin_rationale: Pre-tax margin after credit impairment. FY2022 26.7%, FY2023 27.2%, FY2024 25.6%, FY2025 23.1%, FY2026E ~20.5% (H1 28.0% vs 32.2% a year earlier as impairment rose 20.8%; H2 is seasonally far weaker). Base: credit cost eases from ~1.4% to ~1.15% of loans over four years as the property-developer book runs off, cost-to-income ~36-37% full-year; margin recovers to 26% -- still below FY2022-23, no return to the pre-2020 36-41%.
base.capex_rationale: Equity retained to hold CET1 at 9.4% on RWA growth of 3.0% for five years then 2.5%, from FY2026E RWA ~RMB6,200bn (FY2024 5,843bn, FY2025 6,011bn, H1 2026 6,142bn). RWA growth has been 1.6% (FY2024) and 2.9% (FY2025); 3% is what a ~30% payout on a ~5% ROE can fund. Retention / revenue = g x 0.094 x RWA_prev / revenue = 11.7% (FY2027), 9.8% once growth steps down to the 2.5% terminal rate. Terminal ROE ~5.4% on ordinary equity; implied terminal P/B (ROE - g)/(CoE - g) ~0.34x.
base.tax_rationale: Income tax 5.2% of PBT (FY2025 1,677/32,259; ~6.6% H1 2026 -- very low because government-bond interest is tax-exempt) + NCI ~0% + perpetual-bond coupons ~RMB4.0bn/yr on RMB125bn outstanding (FY2025 3,112 deducted from equity-holder profit; H1 2026 2,190) = ~18.5% of FY2027E PBT. Held flat: the coupon share falls as PBT grows but the effective tax rate rises as the tax-exempt bond income becomes a smaller share; the two roughly offset.
base.terminal_note: Gordon on FY2036 FCFE at 11.0% - 2.5% = 12.1x; the 18x cap does not bind. Terminal growth 2.5% equals terminal RWA growth, so retention and growth are internally consistent (payout = 1 - g/ROE ~54%).
base.narrative: Slow repair: NIM holds ~1.45-1.5%, credit cost eases from ~1.4% to ~1.15%, the balance sheet grows ~3% and the ~30% payout stays covered by FCFE with CET1 flat at 9.4%. ROE climbs from ~4.3% to ~5.4% -- still far below the cost of equity, so the bank stays a sub-book business.

bull.growth_rationale: NIM recovery continues another 5-10bp as high-cost deposits reprice (H1 2026 spread +9bp YoY), corporate loan growth ~5% continues, fee income recovers with wealth management.
bull.margin_rationale: Credit cost falls back toward ~1.0% (retail stress peaks in 2026, property book largely provisioned), cost-to-income ~34%; 30% is between FY2023 (27.2%) and the H1 2025 level (32.2%).
bull.capex_rationale: CET1 held at 9.4% on RWA growth of 3.5% for five years then 3.0%. Terminal ROE ~6.5%.
bull.tax_rationale: Fixed perpetual-bond coupons are a smaller share of a larger PBT.
bull.terminal_note: Gordon 1.03/0.08 = 12.9x FCFE; cap does not bind.
bull.narrative: China's credit cycle turns: NIM keeps recovering, credit cost normalises toward 1.0%, revenue grows ~4% and PBT margin returns to ~30%. ROE ~6.5% -- better, but still below the cost of equity; the upside is from a deeply discounted starting price, not from a re-rating to book.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 18x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Bear 35% (matches 0998.HK, above the house default): ROE has fallen four years running to 4.9%, credit impairment rose 20.8% YoY in H1 2026 and PBT fell 9.5%, retail loans are shrinking with management flagging retail risk, and CET1 is only ~1.7pt above the D-SIB minimum. Base 45%. Bull 20%: the H1 2026 NIM rebound and lower cost-to-income are real but one half-year old, and even the bull case leaves ROE below the cost of equity.
probability_weighted.band_note: House and street coincide (SBC immaterial): the band collapsed, so band_position is null rather than a degenerate 0.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
